comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C121-C123 regarding the absence of large conformational changes upon coactivator binding in S. cerevisiae APC/C, contrasting with human APC/C. Both evaluations support this mechanistic difference based on structural comparisons.

Strong agreement on claims C5, C25-C26, C125-C126, C129-C130, C138 regarding the absence of the auto-inhibitory loop and different phosphorylation-dependent activation mechanism. Both evaluations recognize this as a major mechanistic difference from human APC/C, though OpenEval provides more detailed structural support.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C117-C119 regarding the pre-existing E2-binding conformation in yeast APC/C without coactivator. Both evaluations identify this as a key mechanistic difference from human APC/C, with peer reviewers explicitly highlighting it as an important finding.

Agreement on claims C3, C105-C108, C137 regarding conservation of CDH1 inhibition by phosphorylation. OpenEval provides detailed structural support while peer reviewers affirm the conservation across kingdoms. Both evaluations support these claims.

Divergent evaluations on claims C27-C30 regarding APC/C reconstitution and phosphorylation. OpenEval finds the biochemical and mass spec data well-supported, while peer reviewers raise concerns about phosphorylation validation lacking quantitative robustness, creating uncertainty.

Partial overlap on structural quality claims C31-C32. Both evaluations affirm the high technical quality of cryo-EM structures. Peer review R1 also addresses C21, C33 regarding overall structural determination as a major strength.

Agreement on claims C2, C34-C36 regarding overall conservation of APC/C architecture between yeast and human. Both evaluations support the widespread structural similarities. Peer review also addresses C22, C132 on APC7 absence, which OpenEval covers separately in R6.

Partial overlap on claims C22, C132 regarding absence of APC7 in S. cerevisiae. Both evaluations support this structural difference. OpenEval R6 also addresses C133-C135 on APC7's mammalian function, which peer reviewers treat as background context in R11.

Agreement on claims C133-C135 regarding APC7's role in mammalian brain development. OpenEval treats these as well-supported contextual claims from prior literature, while peer reviewers accept them as established background information without challenge.

Agreement on claims C48-C49 regarding absence of the C-box module in S. cerevisiae. Both evaluations support this structural difference. OpenEval R7 also addresses C50, while peer review R8 includes C56-C57 on APC1 WD40 domain differences.

Partial overlap on claims C56-C57 regarding the six-bladed WD40 domain structure. Both evaluations support the structural observations. OpenEval R8 also addresses C55, C58-C59 with some uncertainty about species-specificity, while peer review accepts the documented differences.

Agreement on claims C111, C136 regarding absence of a specific helix in S. cerevisiae CDH1. Both evaluations support this structural difference. Peer review R6 also addresses broader CDH1 binding features (C102-C104) covered by OpenEval in R5 and R13.

Partial overlap on claims C102-C104 regarding CDH1 binding mode conservation. OpenEval R5 focuses on phosphorylation-dependent inhibition while peer review R6 addresses overall binding site conservation and orientation, with both supporting the structural observations.

Agreement on claims C64, C71-C73 regarding small subunit structures. Both evaluations support the detailed structural analysis. Peer review R9 encompasses broader small subunit analysis (C77-C79, C83-C86, C88-C89) that OpenEval addresses separately in R10, R11, and R12.

Partial overlap on claims C77-C79 regarding APC13 structural conservation. OpenEval R10 provides detailed analysis of APC13 structure and function, while peer review R9 accepts this as part of comprehensive small subunit documentation.

Partial overlap on claims C83-C86 regarding APC9 structure and function. OpenEval R11 details the AlphaFold2-guided modeling and genetic integration, while peer review R9 accepts the small subunit structural analysis without specific concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C88-C89 regarding APC15 structural conservation. OpenEval R12 provides detailed analysis of APC15NTH conservation and MCC regulation, while peer review R9 accepts this within the broader small subunit analysis.

OpenEval R13 addresses claims C98-C101, C112 regarding coactivator binding sites and CDC23 interactions. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims, though they are implicitly accepted within broader structural validation.

OpenEval R15 addresses claims C51-C54 regarding flexibility of platform subunits. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically discusses this flexibility, though it is consistent with accepted cryo-EM observations.

OpenEval R17 marks claim C113 as uncertain/speculative regarding APC9 segment 2 stabilizing CDH1IR binding site. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific claim, suggesting it was not a focus of reviewer concern.

OpenEval R18 marks claim C131 as uncertain regarding alternative phosphorylation-dependent activation mechanisms. This speculation is not specifically addressed in peer review, though the absence of the auto-inhibitory mechanism is well-supported in both evaluations (R4/R4).

OpenEval R19 marks claim C58 as uncertain regarding species-specificity of the six-bladed WD40 structure. Peer reviewers accept the structural observations without questioning the species-specificity claim, treating it as part of documented differences.

OpenEval R20 addresses 37 claims (C1, C6-C20, C37-C38, C45-C47, C60-C63, C95-C97, C99-C100, C105-C106, C110, C114-C116, C120, C124) as well-established background knowledge from prior literature. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this contextual information without specific evaluation.
